$comment: Performance budgets for the Exepad runtime. Edited deliberately; every change is a perf policy decision. Baselines captured 2026-06-15 from a real `pnpm build:sdk` (SDK = apps/runtime/client/public/runtime_assets/dist/index-*.js, 1.67MB raw / 443KB gzip) and the deployed landing fixture (apps a1kguu163). See README.md for the rationale behind each number and `runner.mjs` for how they are enforced.

bytes.$comment: PRIMARY HARD GATE. Deterministic, parse-bound proxy for mobile TBT/LCP. A Lighthouse *score* is download-shaped and noisy; bytes are reproducible build-to-build. These ceilings are set AT the current baseline so they can only ratchet DOWN — the Phase-2 SDK split should drop sdkBytesGzip from 443KB toward ~200KB on core-only pages. The small `tolerance` absorbs minifier non-determinism, not real regressions. Breaching any ceiling FAILS the build.

lighthouse.$comment: SECONDARY / SOFT GATE. Measured, archived, and trend-tracked. Mobile Lighthouse weights TBT 30% / LCP 25% / CLS 25% / FCP 10% / SI 10%. CPU is pinned to 4x slowdown (the real parse cliff). The Perf FLOOR is generous and only fails the build when the score drops BELOW (floor - tolerancePts) — i.e. a structural regression, not +/-3 noise. The metric ceilings are advisory unless `enforceMetricCeilings` is true (default false): they print warnings and land in the report for trend tracking, but do not fail CI on their own.
